samples.summary: The MAX_LIST_LEVEL ceiling now fails open for non-finite / out-of-band `listLevel` values, so a level poisoned via the unvalidated collaborative ingest path lets a normal indent gesture push items past the ceiling without bound and write `NaN` levels across a whole run of neighbours.
samples.evidence:
Both new guards are plain comparisons against a value that is never validated to be a finite number:
- `subtreeOf` line 37: `if (nextLevel <= level) break;` — if the root's `listLevel` is `NaN`, every comparison is false, so the "subtree" swallows the entire following run of list-items instead of stopping at the first same-or-shallower one.
- `planSiblingGroup` line 74: `if (delta > 0 && deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) continue;` — `deepest = Math.max(deepest, NaN)` is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 8` is false, so the refusal is skipped and line 79 writes `(listLevel ?? 0) + 1` for every member.

Concrete chain: a collaborator (only needs edit access to the shared doc) sends a Yorkie tree block attribute `listLevel: "foo"` (attrs are stringified on the way out at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 and parsed with a bare `Number()` on the way in at packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495 — no `Number.isFinite`, no clamp). The victim's document now holds `listLevel = NaN` on that block. When the victim puts the caret on it and presses Tab / Cmd+], the two guards above both fail open, so: (a) the poisoned item's own level is written back as `NaN`, (b) a following child that was legitimately at level 8 is written to 9, and repeated presses drive it to 10, 11, … past the documented ceiling, and (c) the walk carries an arbitrarily long run of unrelated items. The old per-block code this hunk deletes (`if (currentLevel >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) return;` in editor.ts/text-editor.ts/text-box-editor.ts) evaluated the clamp against each written block, so the level-8 member was refused; the subtree-level check re-derives the decision from a value the attacker controls. Downstream, layout multiplies the level directly (`LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` at packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494 and table-layout.ts:93), so a `NaN`/unbounded level turns into a `NaN` or enormous available width in the wrapper — degraded or hung rendering for everyone who opens the doc, and the corruption is persisted back through the CRDT to all peers. Minimal fix: coerce with `Number.isFinite(...) ? Math.min(MAX_LIST_LEVEL, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(v))) : 0` where the level is read in this module (and ideally at the CRDT parse sites), so the guard cannot be short-circuited by a hostile value.

samples.summary: `listLevel` arriving from the collaborative (Yorkie tree attribute) path is parsed with a bare `Number()` — no finite check, no 0..MAX_LIST_LEVEL clamp — even though the clipboard path validates and clamps the identical field, and the new module now declares MAX_LIST_LEVEL as the model invariant.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:348-351 validates untrusted pasted input (`asNumber` rejects non-finite at clipboard.ts:69-71, then `Math.min(MAX_LIST_LEVEL, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(level)))`). The remote-collaboration ingest does not: packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 `if ('listLevel' in attrs) block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel);` and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495 `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel);`. Serialization (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178) is `String(block.listLevel)` with no schema validation, so any peer can put `"NaN"`, `"1e9"` or `"-5"` on the wire. Nothing between the wire and the editor re-clamps, which is what makes the guard bypass in finding #1 reachable, and what lets a hostile level reach layout's `LIST_INDENT_PX * (level + 1)` multiplication (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494). Impact is bounded because the actor already has write access to the document, so this is data-integrity/resource abuse rather than privilege escalation. The new `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` export is the natural place to hang a shared `sanitizeListLevel()` used by both the clipboard and the two CRDT readers.

samples.summary: `changes.push(...planSiblingGroup(...))` spreads a caller-sized array into arguments, which throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` once a plan exceeds the engine's argument limit — a select-all indent on a pathologically large pasted/synced list crashes the editor mid-gesture, after `docStore.snapshot()` but before any write.
samples.evidence: Line 116 spreads the whole per-group plan. A document whose list run is large enough (roughly >100k planned blocks in V8) makes the spread throw rather than the loop merely being slow; the throw escapes `applyListLevelChanges` inside `indent()`/`handleTab`, so the gesture aborts with a snapshot already taken. Document size is attacker-influenceable through paste (clipboard.ts sanitizes shape but not block count) or through the CRDT sync path. Pure availability hardening: `for (const c of planSiblingGroup(...)) changes.push(c);` removes the cliff.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. list-level.ts:30-39 seeds `level`/`deepest` from an unvalidated `listLevel ?? 0` (which does not catch NaN), and both ceiling guards are plain comparisons: line 37 `if (nextLevel <= level) break;` and line 74 `if (delta > 0 && deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) continue;`. Both are false for NaN, so the subtree walk swallows the whole following list run and the MAX_LIST_LEVEL refusal is skipped, with line 79 writing `(listLevel ?? 0) + delta` for every member — including a member legitimately at level 8. The module has no Number.isFinite or clamp. The untrusted ingest path is also real: crdt-tree.ts:243 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:494-496 both parse the wire attribute with a bare `Number()` with no finiteness check or clamp, while attrs are stringified on the way out (backend docs-tree.ts:178, yorkie-doc-store.ts:371), so a peer writing `listLevel: "foo"` lands NaN in the victim's document. The codebase validates comparable numeric attrs elsewhere (clipboard.ts:348-351 clamps a pasted level; crdt-attrs.ts:97,138,177 gate on Number.isFinite), confirming the omission is a gap rather than an upstream contract. Downstream impact is if anything stronger than claimed: layout.ts:1091 assigns `Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` to Array.length, which throws RangeError for NaN and allocates proportionally for a large finite level, and layout.ts:494 / table-layout.ts:93 multiply the level into marginLeft. I found no normalization between the parse sites and planListLevelChanges (callers editor.ts:1603, text-editor.ts:2720, text-box-editor.ts:829 apply changes verbatim), so nothing makes it unreachable. I weighed an out-of-scope refutation (authorized collaborator; formatting ceiling is not a permission gate) but rejected it: this is unvalidated attacker-controlled data crossing a peer trust boundary, persistently corrupting every other client's render, which is in the unsafe-input-handling lane.
